subject: Availability measurement, sampling policy & temporary exception matrix
messages:
From: Sally Chen <sally@greenline.health>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenLine SRE <sre@greenline.health>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement question: how you measure availability & temporary exceptions

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week — GreenLine is very interested in Redwood for inference serving. Our procurement team asked for a brief write-up of how you measure availability and latency SLOs, plus:

- Exact metrics you use for availability (windows, probe vs. real traffic).
- How you sample production traffic for latency SLOs and whether that impacts billing.
- The alerting thresholds / on-call flow we should expect.
- What customers get access to (dashboards, raw telemetry, synthetic probes).
- Your process for temporary SLO exceptions (for planned migrations, rollouts, or incident remediation) — who approves, typical durations, and post-mortem requirements.

If you have a short matrix or template we can attach to our procurement packet, that would help speed review.

Appreciate it — can we aim to have something by EOD Thursday (16 Sep)?

Best,
Sally
Sally Chen
Director, Platform Ops
GreenLine Health

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Chen <sally@greenline.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement question: how you measure availability & temporary exceptions

Hi Sally — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary and we'll attach a one-page matrix for your packet. Karthik and Marissa are looped for technical and procurement notes.

Overview (short):
- Availability definition: we measure "service availability" as the percent of successful inference responses within the configured latency SLO window over a 30d rolling window (default). Success = HTTP 200 with valid model output; failures include HTTP 5xx, timeouts, and explicit "capacity_exceeded" errors.
- Measurement windows: rolling 30d primary SLO; supporting 7d and 1d windows for operational alerts. For contractual uptime (SLA), we report 30d and monthly aggregates.
- Latency SLOs: we expose p50/p95/p99 for token latency and end-to-end request latency. Contracts typically tie a p99 request latency (at a configured payload seq length) to a threshold (e.g., p99 < 350ms) — we provide the measurement artifact showing the sequence-length distribution we used.
- Sampling: production sampling is stratified: 100% of synthetic probes; 10% of live-requests by default for detailed traces; aggregated latency histograms are computed on 100% of requests at a lightweight histogram resolution (no payload capture by default). Sampling rate is configurable per customer and per route. Sampling does not affect billing — we bill on tokens consumed, independent of telemetry sampling.
- Synthetic probes: we run regional synthetic probes (per-region, per-model) every minute for availability and warm-start latency baselines; these are visible in the read-only dashboard.
- Alerting: critical alerts fire on service-level indicators (error-rate > X over 15m or p99 degradation > Y). Pager escalation is standard SRE: on-call -> follow-up -> incident commander. We provide an on-call contact for Dedicated/Private customers and a runbook.
- Customer access: read-only Grafana dashboard (per-route, per-model), daily SLO reports (csv), and an optional metrics-stream (Prometheus remote_write or S3 export) for enterprise customers.
- Temporary exceptions: requested via a formal "exception request" form (we've attached a template). Approval path: SRE (technical) + Procurement (commercial) for exceptions >72 hours. Typical approvals: routine rollouts — up to 7 days; migrations or major upgrades require a remediation plan and an RCA within 7 days after the exception ends. Exceptions are limited, logged, and timeboxed.

I'll attach: 1) exception-matrix.xlsx (fields: impact, max duration, approvers, rollback criteria), 2) slo-metrics-appendix.pdf (methodology), and 3) grafana-invite-link.txt with the read-only URL.

Marissa — procurement/contract note: we should confirm whether GreenLine needs raw telemetry exports or only the read-only dashboards and daily CSV — that affects the procurement clause on data retention.

Sally — happy to hop on a 30-minute call if your procurement team prefers a walkthrough.

Thanks,
Markus
VP Product
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: slo-metrics-appendix.pdf, exception-matrix.xlsx, grafana-invite-link.txt]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement question: how you measure availability & temporary exceptions

Sally — quick technical clarifications to supplement Markus' note:

- Error classification: we tag errors with categories (infrastructure, model, input validation). SLOs use a failure boolean that counts all categories except "client_cancelled" for availability metrics.
- Histogram buckets: we use HDR histograms on the service side; stored p99 is computed from those buckets (no request body storage).
- Sampling for traces: the 10% default is applied uniformly across routes, but customers can request route-specific overrides (we've done this for high-volume inference routes to reduce noise).
- Impact windows: for exception approvals, we require a pre-deployment test run (synthetic-run) showing failure-mode behavior and a rollback plan; exceptions longer than 24 hours must include an automated rollback criterion.
- Data access options: for Prometheus remote_write we require a VPN peering or whitelisted IPs for Dedicated/Private; hosted customers get read-only Grafana and CSV exports.

I've uploaded a draft exception matrix and a short runbook excerpt to the procurement folder. Link: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1A2b_ProcurementPackets_GL-089

-Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: exception-matrix.xlsx]

Hi Sally — Procurement here. Quick commercial clarifications so your packaging team can slot this into the SOW:

1) Exception durations and credits: exceptions we approve don't automatically generate credits; credits are only triggered for SLA breaches as defined in the SOW. We will record approved exceptions in the contract appendix so audit parties are aware.

2) Access tiers: by default hosted customers receive read-only Grafana + daily SLO csv; Dedicated includes configurable remote_write and a one-time integration window to set up peering. Private (on-prem) customers control telemetry locally.

3) Deliverables: when an exception is requested we will provide: exception approval ticket, expected end time, rollback criteria, and an RCA within 7 days. Please let me know if GreenLine requires an alternate SLA credit language.

If EOD Thursday still works, we can hand over the exception-matrix.xlsx (attached) plus the SLO methodology appendix as a single packet.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
